title: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
syllabus: Photosynthesis as a means of autotrophic nutrition; Site of photosynthesis; Pigments involved in photosynthesis (elementary idea); Photochemical and biosynthetic phases of photosynthesis; Cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation; Chemiosmotic hypothesis; Photorespiration; C3 and C4 pathways; Factors affecting photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following scientists demonstrated that oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) and not from carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$), based on studies with purple and green sulphur bacteria?
questions.solution: Cornelius van Niel (a microbiologist) demonstrated that photosynthesis is essentially a light-dependent reaction in which hydrogen from an oxidisable compound reduces carbon dioxide to carbohydrates. In green plants, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is the hydrogen donor and is oxidised to $\text{O}_2$.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the photosynthetic pigments and their characteristic chromatographic colours:

List-I (Pigment)List-II (Colour in Chromatogram)
(A) Chlorophyll a(I) Yellow-green
(B) Chlorophyll b(II) Yellow
(C) Xanthophylls(III) Bright or blue-green
(D) Carotenoids(IV) Yellow to yellow-orange

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: A chromatographic separation of leaf pigments shows: Chlorophyll a appears as bright or blue-green, Chlorophyll b as yellow-green, Xanthophylls as yellow, and Carotenoids as yellow to yellow-orange.

questions.question: The reaction centre chlorophyll a molecules in Photosystem I (PS I) and Photosystem II (PS II) have absorption maxima at which wavelengths respectively?
questions.solution: The reaction centre of PS I is known as $\text{P}_{700}$ because its absorption peak is at $700\text{ nm}$, whereas the reaction centre of PS II is $\text{P}_{680}$ because its absorption maxima is at $680\text{ nm}$ (in the red region).

questions.question: The water-splitting complex (oxygen-evolving complex) is associated with which photosystem and located on which side of the thylakoid membrane?
options: PS II, located on the inner side (lumen side) of the thylakoid membrane
PS I, located on the outer side (stroma side) of the thylakoid membrane
PS II, located on the outer side (stroma side) of the thylakoid membrane
PS I, located in the stroma lamellae
questions.solution: The water-splitting complex is physically associated with PS II and is located on the inner side (lumenal surface) of the thylakoid membrane. As water is split, protons and oxygen are released into the thylakoid lumen.

questions.question: Which of the following mineral ions are catalytically essential for the photolysis of water during the light reaction of photosynthesis?
questions.solution: Manganese ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$) and Chloride ($\text{Cl}^-$) ions are essential for the oxygen-evolving complex during the photolysis of water: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 4\text{H}^+ + \text{O}_2 + 4e^-$.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Cyclic Photophosphorylation:
Statement I: It occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond $680\text{ nm}$ are available for excitation.
Statement II: It results only in the synthesis of $\text{ATP}$, but not $\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+$.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. In the stroma lamellae (which lack PS II and NADP reductase), when light beyond $680\text{ nm}$ is available, only PS I operates cyclically, synthesizing only $\text{ATP}$ without photolysis of water or $\text{NADPH}$ formation.

questions.question: According to Mitchell's Chemiosmotic Hypothesis, which of the following causes the development of a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane during light reactions?
options: Accumulation of protons inside the thylakoid lumen and removal of protons from the stroma
Accumulation of protons in the stroma and depletion in the lumen
Direct pumping of $\text{ATP}$ from stroma into the lumen
Active export of $\text{NADPH}$ into the intermembrane space
questions.solution: A proton gradient develops with high $[\text{H}^+]$ inside the lumen and low $[\text{H}^+]$ in the stroma due to: (1) water splitting on the lumen side, (2) proton translocation across the membrane by plastoquinone, and (3) proton consumption in the stroma by $\text{NADP}^+$ reductase.

questions.question: The catalytic component $F_1$ of $\text{ATP}$ synthase (CF0-CF1 complex) in chloroplasts is located on the:
options: Inner surface facing the thylakoid lumen
Embedded completely within the lipid bilayer
Outer membrane of the chloroplast envelope
questions.solution: CF0 is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and forms a transmembrane proton channel, whereas the CF1 headpiece protrudes into the stroma and catalyzes $\text{ATP}$ synthesis when protons flow down the electrochemical gradient.

questions.question: The primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor in the Calvin cycle ($	ext{C}_3$ pathway) is a:
questions.solution: Melvin Calvin discovered that the primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor in the $	ext{C}_3$ cycle is a 5-carbon ketose sugar called ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the three distinct stages of the Calvin cycle:

List-I (Stage)List-II (Key Chemical Event)
(A) Carboxylation(I) Consumption of $2\text{ ATP}$ and $2\text{ NADPH}$ per $\text{CO}_2$ fixed
(B) Reduction(II) Fixation of $\text{CO}_2$ into two molecules of $3\text{-PGA}$ via RuBisCO
(C) Regeneration(III) Consumption of $1\text{ ATP}$ for phosphorylation to reform RuBP

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Carboxylation: Fixation of $\text{CO}_2$ with RuBP to form $2$ molecules of $3\text{-PGA}$; Reduction: Requires $2\text{ ATP}$ and $2\text{ NADPH}$ per $\text{CO}_2$ molecule; Regeneration: Requires $1\text{ ATP}$ to regenerate the $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor RuBP.

questions.question: To synthesize ONE molecule of glucose via the $	ext{C}_3$ pathway (Calvin cycle), the total requirements of $\text{ATP}$ and $\text{NADPH}$ are:
questions.solution: For each $\text{CO}_2$ fixed, $3\text{ ATP}$ and $2\text{ NADPH}$ are required. Therefore, for 6 turns of the cycle to produce 1 glucose molecule ($6\text{ CO}_2$): $6 \times 3 = 18\text{ ATP}$ and $6 \times 2 = 12\text{ NADPH}$.

questions.question: The primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor in $	ext{C}_4$ plants is ________ and the enzyme catalyzing this initial fixation in mesophyll cells is ________:
questions.solution: In $	ext{C}_4$ plants (e.g., Maize, Sugarcane), the primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule, phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), present in mesophyll cells, and the reaction is catalyzed by PEP carboxylase (PEPcase).

questions.question: Kranz anatomy is a characteristic anatomical feature of $	ext{C}_4$ leaves. The bundle sheath cells surrounding the vascular bundles in $	ext{C}_4$ plants are characterized by having:
options: Large numbers of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, and no intercellular spaces
Few chloroplasts with thin cellulosic walls and large intercellular spaces
High concentration of PEPcase and absence of RuBisCO
Abundant stomata and thin non-suberized walls
questions.solution: Bundle sheath cells of $	ext{C}_4$ plants have a 'Kranz' (wreath) arrangement characterized by several layers of cells with thick walls impervious to gases, no intercellular spaces, and numerous agranal chloroplasts rich in RuBisCO.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the cellular compartments and steps of the $ ext{C}_4$ (Hatch and Slack) pathway:

List-I (Step / Reaction)List-II (Site / Enzyme)
(A) Primary $\text{CO}_2$ fixation forming OAA(I) Bundle sheath cells via decarboxylase
(B) Decarboxylation releasing $\text{CO}_2$ and $C_3$ acid(II) Mesophyll cells via PEPcase
(C) Calvin cycle ($ ext{C}_3$) operation(III) Mesophyll cells consuming $2\text{ ATP}$ equivalents
(D) Regeneration of PEP from pyruvate(IV) Bundle sheath cells via RuBisCO

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Primary fixation: Mesophyll cells via PEPcase; Decarboxylation: Bundle sheath cells; Calvin cycle: Bundle sheath cells containing RuBisCO; Regeneration of PEP from pyruvate: Mesophyll cells.

questions.question: How many total $\text{ATP}$ and $\text{NADPH}$ molecules are consumed to produce ONE molecule of hexose sugar (glucose) in $	ext{C}_4$ plants?
questions.solution: In $	ext{C}_4$ plants, fixing each $\text{CO}_2$ requires $2\text{ ATP}$ for the $	ext{C}_4$ cycle and $3\text{ ATP} + 2\text{ NADPH}$ for the $	ext{C}_3$ cycle ($5\text{ ATP} + 2\text{ NADPH}$ per $\text{CO}_2$). For 1 glucose ($6\text{ CO}_2$), the total requirement is $30\text{ ATP}$ and $12\text{ NADPH}$.

questions.question: Photorespiration (the $	ext{C}_2$ cycle) is initiated when RuBisCO acts as an oxygenase under conditions of:
options: High $\text{O}_2$ concentration, low $\text{CO}_2$ concentration, high temperature, and high light intensity
High $\text{CO}_2$ concentration, low $\text{O}_2$, and low temperature
questions.solution: RuBisCO has an affinity for both $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$. When $[\text{O}_2]$ is high and $[\text{CO}_2]$ is low, and at elevated temperatures, oxygen binds to the active site of RuBisCO, initiating the wasteful photorespiratory pathway.

questions.question: When RuBisCO functions as an oxygenase in $	ext{C}_3$ plants, RuBP ($5\text{C}$) is cleaved into:
options: One molecule of 3-PGA ($3\text{C}$) and one molecule of 2-Phosphoglycolate ($2\text{C}$)
One molecule of OAA ($4\text{C}$) and one molecule of $\text{CO}_2$
questions.solution:
$$\text{RuBP (5C)} + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{RuBisCO}} \text{3-PGA (3C)} + \text{2-Phosphoglycolate (2C)}$$
Phosphoglycolate is dephosphorylated to glycolate and enters the photorespiratory cycle.

questions.question: Photorespiration does NOT occur in $	ext{C}_4$ plants because:
options: They possess a mechanism that increases the $\text{CO}_2$ concentration at the RuBisCO enzyme site in bundle sheath cells
Their RuBisCO enzyme is structurally modified to bind only $\text{CO}_2$
They completely lack the enzyme RuBisCO
They do not split water during photosynthesis
questions.solution: In $	ext{C}_4$ plants, malate/aspartate is transported to bundle sheath cells and decarboxylated, releasing a high concentration of $\text{CO}_2$ around RuBisCO. This minimizes oxygenase activity and prevents photorespiration.

questions.question: Which of the following three cell organelles participate cooperatively in the photorespiratory ($	ext{C}_2$) cycle?
options: Chloroplast, Golgi body, and Endoplasmic reticulum
questions.solution: Photorespiration involves three organelles in sequence: Chloroplast (formation of glycolate) $\to$ Peroxisome (oxidation to glyoxylate and transamination to glycine) $\to$ Mitochondria (two glycines form one serine, releasing $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{NH}_3$).

questions.question: Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors (1905) states that:
options: If a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, its rate is determined by the factor that is nearest to its minimal value
Photosynthesis rate is determined solely by the factor present in maximum abundance
Light intensity always limits photosynthesis at noon
Temperature has no effect on photosynthetic enzymes
questions.solution: F.F. Blackman (1905) formulated the Law of Limiting Factors: 'If a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, then its rate will be determined by the factor which is nearest to its minimal value: it is the factor which directly affects the process if its quantity is changed.'

questions.question: Light saturation for photosynthesis typically occurs at what percentage of full sunlight?
questions.solution: Except for plants in shade or in dense forests, light is rarely a limiting factor in nature because light saturation occurs at about $10\%$ of full sunlight.

questions.question: The $\text{CO}_2$ saturation levels for $	ext{C}_3$ and $	ext{C}_4$ plants occur at approximately:
questions.solution: $\text{C}_4$ plants show $\text{CO}_2$ saturation at about $360\,\mu\text{L/L}$ ($360\text{ ppm}$), whereas $	ext{C}_3$ plants respond to increased $[\text{CO}_2]$ and saturation is seen only beyond $450\,\mu\text{L/L}$ ($450\text{ ppm}$).

questions.question: Greenhouse crops such as tomatoes and bell peppers are grown in $\text{CO}_2$-enriched atmospheres because:
options: They are $\text{C}_3$ plants that show higher photosynthetic rates and yield under elevated $\text{CO}_2$ ($	ext{CO}_2$ fertilization effect)
They are $\text{C}_4$ plants that require high temperatures
questions.solution: Tomatoes and bell peppers are $\text{C}_3$ plants. Since current atmospheric $[\text{CO}_2]$ ($\,\approx 400\text{ ppm}$) is sub-saturating for $	ext{C}_3$ plants, growing them in $\text{CO}_2$-enriched greenhouse atmospheres ($500-600\text{ ppm}$) increases photosynthesis and crop productivity.

questions.question: The primary electron acceptor that accepts an excited electron from the reaction centre $\text{P}_{680}$ in Photosystem II is:
questions.solution: When $\text{P}_{680}$ absorbs light, it excites an electron that is accepted by the primary electron acceptor, pheophytin (a modified chlorophyll a molecule lacking $\text{Mg}^{2+}$), which passes it to plastoquinone.

questions.question: Plastocyanin is a small, mobile, copper-containing peripheral membrane protein that transfers electrons from:
options: Cytochrome $b_6f$ complex to $\text{P}_{700}$ of PS I
questions.solution: Plastocyanin (PC) is a water-soluble copper-containing protein located on the lumenal surface of the thylakoid membrane that mediates electron transfer from the cytochrome $b_6f$ complex to the oxidized $\text{P}_{700}^+$ reaction centre of PS I.

questions.question: The enzyme $\text{NADP}^+$ reductase is located on which side of the chloroplast thylakoid membrane?
options: Outer surface (stromal side) of the thylakoid membrane
Inner surface (lumen side) of the thylakoid membrane
questions.solution: The enzyme ferredoxin-NADP reductase (FNR) is located on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane. It transfers electrons from reduced ferredoxin to $\text{NADP}^+$, consuming a stromal proton to generate $\text{NADPH}$.

questions.question: Stroma lamellae membranes (unstacked thylakoids) lack which of the following complexes?
options: Photosystem II (PS II) and $\text{NADP}$ reductase enzyme
questions.solution: The stroma lamellae (intergranal thylakoids) contain only PS I and $\text{ATP}$ synthase; they lack PS II and the enzyme $\text{NADP}$ reductase, which is why only cyclic photophosphorylation can take place in these regions.

questions.question: T.W. Engelmann (1843–1909) plotted the first action spectrum of photosynthesis by illuminating the green alga Cladophora using a prism and observing the accumulation of aerobic bacteria in regions of:
questions.solution: Engelmann split light using a prism to illuminate Cladophora in a suspension of aerobic bacteria. The bacteria accumulated mainly in the regions of blue and red light, describing the first action spectrum of photosynthesis (which resembles the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a and b).

questions.question: In $	ext{C}_4$ plants, the first stable product of photosynthetic $\text{CO}_2$ fixation is:
questions.solution: In $	ext{C}_4$ plants, $\text{CO}_2$ is initially fixed in mesophyll cells by PEPcase to form the 4-carbon dicarboxylic acid, oxaloacetic acid (OAA), which is subsequently converted to malic acid or aspartic acid.

questions.question: During the Z-scheme of non-cyclic electron transport, the movement of electrons from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{NADP}^+$ is:
options: Uphill to primary acceptor, downhill through ETS, uphill to PS I acceptor, and downhill to $\text{NADP}^+$
Uphill entirely requiring continuous ATP hydrolysis
questions.solution: Electrons move uphill in redox potential from $\text{P}_{680}$ to the primary electron acceptor, then downhill along an electron transport chain to PS I ($\,\text{P}_{700}$), uphill to the PS I acceptor, and finally downhill to $\text{NADP}^+$ to form $\text{NADPH}$ (forming the characteristic Z-scheme).

questions.question: Which of the following is an accessory photosynthetic pigment that protects chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation (solarization)?
questions.solution: Carotenoids (carotenes and xanthophylls) are accessory pigments that absorb light and transfer energy to chlorophyll a while also protecting the photosynthetic apparatus from photo-oxidation under excess light.

questions.question: The enzymatic reactions of the dark reaction (biosynthetic phase) take place in the:
questions.solution: The light reactions (photochemical phase) occur in the thylakoid membranes, whereas the dark reactions (biosynthetic phase/Calvin cycle), which use the $\text{ATP}$ and $\text{NADPH}$ produced during the light reactions, take place in the stroma of the chloroplast.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is a typical $	ext{C}_4$ plant?
questions.solution: Maize, Sugarcane, Sorghum, and Amaranthus are typical $	ext{C}_4$ plants adapted to dry tropical regions. Wheat, Rice, and Potato are $	ext{C}_3$ plants.

questions.question: During photorespiration, which gas is consumed and which gas is released without the production of $\text{ATP}$ or $\text{NADPH}$?
questions.solution: Photorespiration is a wasteful process in which $\text{O}_2$ is consumed (in chloroplast and peroxisome) and $\text{CO}_2$ is released (in mitochondria) with the consumption of $\text{ATP}$, producing no energy-rich molecules.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the temperature sensitivity of photosynthesis:
Statement I: The dark reactions (biosynthetic phase) being enzymatic are much more temperature-sensitive than the light reactions.
Statement II: $ ext{C}_4$ plants have a higher temperature optimum than $ ext{C}_3$ plants.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The dark reactions are purely enzymatic and sensitive to temperature changes. $	ext{C}_4$ plants (adapted to tropical climates) have an optimum temperature of $30-45^\circ\text{C}$, while $	ext{C}_3$ plants have an optimum around $20-25^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.question: The radioactive isotope used by Melvin Calvin and his co-workers to map the complete pathway of carbon fixation in green algae (Chlorella and Scenedesmus) was:
questions.solution: Melvin Calvin used radioactive $^{14}\text{C}$ (carbon-14) in algal photosynthetic studies, leading to the discovery that the first $\text{CO}_2$ fixation product in $	ext{C}_3$ plants is 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA).

questions.question: When electrons pass through the Cytochrome $b_6f$ complex from plastoquinone to plastocyanin, the protons pumped across the membrane into the lumen come from the:
questions.solution: Plastoquinone (PQ) acts as a hydrogen carrier. As it accepts electrons from PS II, it picks up protons from the stroma. Upon oxidation by the Cytochrome $b_6f$ complex, PQ releases protons into the thylakoid lumen.

questions.question: The enzyme RuBisCO comprises approximately what percentage of total soluble leaf protein in green plants?
questions.solution: RuBisCO is the most abundant protein on Earth, constituting about $16\%$ to over $40\%$ of the total soluble protein in photosynthetic plant leaves.

questions.question: In green sulfur bacteria, the hydrogen donor for carbon reduction during photosynthesis is:
questions.solution: Purple and green sulfur bacteria perform anoxygenic photosynthesis using $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ (or thiosulfate) as the hydrogen donor instead of water, liberating sulfur or sulfate instead of $\text{O}_2$.

questions.question: Water stress in plants causes stomatal closure, which reduces photosynthetic rate primarily by:
options: Decreasing $\text{CO}_2$ availability and reducing leaf surface area through wilting
Halving the amount of water needed for photolysis
questions.solution: Water stress leads to stomatal closure, sharply reducing the internal availability of $\text{CO}_2$. In addition, leaf wilting decreases the surface area available for light interception.

questions.question: The optimum temperature for photosynthesis in $	ext{C}_3$ and $	ext{C}_4$ plants is approximately:
questions.solution: $	ext{C}_3$ plants have a lower temperature optimum ($20-25^\circ\text{C}$), whereas tropical $	ext{C}_4$ plants operate optimally at higher temperatures ($30-45^\circ\text{C}$).

questions.question: In the light reaction of photosynthesis, the movement of electrons through the electron transport chain releases energy that is utilized to pump protons ($H^+$) into the:
questions.solution: Energy released by electrons as they pass down the electron transport chain is coupled to the transport of protons from the stroma into the thylakoid lumen.

questions.question: Which of the following photosynthetic pigments is considered the universal primary pigment present in all oxygenic photosynthetic organisms?
questions.solution: Chlorophyll a is the essential primary photosynthetic pigment found in all oxygen-evolving photosynthetic autotrophs (cyanobacteria, algae, and higher plants), functioning as the reaction centre.

questions.question: How many molecules of $\text{CO}_2$ must enter the Calvin cycle to produce one molecule of 3-carbon triose phosphate (Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate)?
questions.solution: Fixation of 3 molecules of $\text{CO}_2$ (3 turns of the Calvin cycle) yields 6 molecules of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P), of which 5 are recycled to regenerate 3 RuBP molecules, leaving a net gain of 1 triose phosphate ($3\text{C}$).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the landmark experiments in photosynthesis:

List-I (Scientist)List-II (Key Discovery)
(A) Joseph Priestley (1770)(I) Sunlight is essential; green plant parts release oxygen bubbles
(B) Jan Ingenhousz (1779)(II) Plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove
(C) Julius von Sachs (1854)(III) Hydroponics and evidence that glucose is produced and stored as starch

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Priestley (1770): Bell jar experiment showing plants restore foul air; Ingenhousz (1779): Showed that sunlight is essential and green parts release $\text{O}_2$ bubbles; Julius von Sachs (1854): Showed that green parts make glucose, which is stored as starch.
